newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 28.

text.p: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BRUSSELS MAY BAR ANGLO-LONRHO DEAL Anglo-American's

plans to acquire a substantial stake in South African mining house Lonrho may be blocked by the European Commission. Last year European competition commissioner Karel Van Miert blocked a proposed merger between Lonhro's platinum division and Impala, a subsidiary of South African group Gencor, for fear of creating a virtual monopoly in the platinum market. Similar fears are behind the Commission's objections to the deal with Anglo-American.

-- BLAIR GETS HIS FEET UNDER THE TABLE WITH BUSINESS The bosses of some of Britain's biggest companies gathered at a breakfast reception at the Midland Bank's City headquarters to listen to addresses by Labour party leader Tony Blair and shadow chancellor Gordon Brown. This was the most important event yet in Labour's campaign to win the support of the business community. Chairmen and chief executives of about 50 companies attended, including Lord Sterling of P&O and Christopher Haskins of Northern Foods.

-- PUTTING A PRICE ON BT'S HALO EFFECT, The telecommunications regulatory body Oftel has issued a consultative paper proposing that British Telecommunications offer a universal service scheme. Oftel's director general Don Cruickshank argues that BT's dominant and ubiquitous position in the market, which brings it certain benefits, obliges it to provide such a service. Under Mr Cruickshank's proposals BT's competitors would contribute to a fund to compensate BT for the cost of maintaining the service.

-- ABBEY NATIONAL SUFFERS LOSS OF HOME LOAN SHARE Abbey National Building Society is putting its hopes in a predicted 12 per cent upturn in house purchases falling a fall in its share of new home loans. Despite the acquisition of the National & Provincial Building Society last year, Abbey's share of the home loan market in the UK last year fell to 5.9 per cent. The company also announced pre-tax profits, up 14 per cent to 1.17 billion sterling despite 61 million of additional costs for the integration of N&P.

-- HTV SET TO CLINCH PRODUCTION DEAL WITH WARNER Extensive negotiations between US media giant Warner Brothers and HTV, the independent television company for Wales and the west of England, are believed to be near completion. A deal would mean that HTV, one of the last sizeable ITV companies not to be acquired by larger groups, would be Warners preferred production partner in the UK.
-- BRITISH GAS BOWS OUT WITH 1 BILLION STERLING CHARGE British

Gas, which is preparing to demerge, has reported a net loss of 178 million sterling thanks largely to 1.4 billion sterling of exceptional charges. These charges mainly relate to take-or-pay contracts with North Sea gas producers which committed British Gas to buy gas it no longer needs at a price well above market rates. British Gas operating profits rose to 1.33 billion sterling last year, however its exploration and production division reported a 68 million sterling loss.

-- BRITISH LAND TO RUN GUS'S PROPERTY Great Universal Stores and British Land have announced the creation of a new group to run the retail group's investment property portfolio. The joint venture company, to be called BL Universal, will own 982 high street and shopping centre properties. -- SB IN RESEARCH PARTNERSHIPS Anglo-American pharmaceutical group SmithKline Beecham has announced a research partnership with two biotechnology companies, Cadus Pharmaceutical of the U.S. and Evotec BioSystems of Germany. SB president Jean-Pierre Garnier said that both alliances were aimed at accelerating the discovery of new drugs with particular emphasis on genomics - the study of how genes cause disease.
-- LASMO SPENDS 25 MILLION STERLING ON OIL PRICE HEDGE

The UK's second largest oil exploration company Lasmo have reported a rise in annual net profits to 67 million sterling. This figure could have been higher but for the 25 million sterling cost incurred in hedging policies aimed at protecting the company against a collapse in oil prices. -- PARTCO EXPANDS VIA 103 MILLION STERLING DEAL The UK's largest vehicle parts distributor Partco is to acquire car parts company Dana Distribution Europe. Partco will pay Dana's parent company, Dana Corporation of the US, 103 million sterling. The Office of Fair Trading has invited comment on the deal which would give Partco a 13 per cent share of the UK car parts distribution market. For a full range of news monitoring services.
